{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — Master Services Agreement

**To:** Deal team 
**From:** In-house counsel (Customer side) 
**Re:** Playbook review of the Master Services Agreement — verified findings

---

## Executive summary

We reviewed the Master Services Agreement against the playbook and identified **eight deviations** (two critical, four high, two medium), **nine compliant clauses**, and **one item requiring internal review**.

The agreement is unusually one-sided in a small number of clauses, several of which contradict other clauses that are already acceptable to us. The two critical items are the indemnity and liability provisions: Section 20 contains a single one-way indemnity running from Customer to Vendor with **no Vendor indemnity anywhere** (and Section 9.3 cross-references a non-existent "Section 20.5"), and Section 21.1 caps liability at **one month of Fees paid "without exception"**, pulling the Section 21.3 Excluded Claims inside the cap and contradicting Section 21.2.

Four high-severity deviations impose restrictions on us that sit in walk-away territory and conflict with Section 12.3, in which Vendor expressly acknowledges that Customer has made no exclusivity, non-compete or minimum-volume commitment: a full-term sole-source obligation (§ 2.2), a three-year USD 2,000,000/year take-or-pay commitment "without reduction or termination rights" (§ 2.1), a 24-month worldwide post-term non-compete (§ 12.4), and a Services licence that is revocable at Vendor's discretion and excludes our Affiliates and contractors (§ 13.1, contradicting §§ 13.2–13.3). Two medium deviations remain: § 11.1 mandates immediate cessation of assistance and permanent deletion of Customer Data (contradicting §§ 11.2–11.3), and § 19.2 limits the Deliverable warranty to fifteen days and cuts off the § 19.1 warranty and § 19.4 remedies.

Much of the agreement is favourable and needs no redline, including IP and Customer Data ownership (§§ 14–15), assignment and change of control (§ 24), termination for convenience (§ 9.4), audit rights (§ 22), governing law and venue (§ 28), auto-renewal and price uplift (§§ 8.2–8.3), and Vendor insurance (§ 18). Several of the deviations can be repaired with single-paragraph edits that simply conform the offending clause to language Vendor has already agreed elsewhere in the document.

---

## Findings

| Severity | Rule | Status | Section |
|---|---|---|---|
| Critical | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | Deviation | § 20 (20.1); cross-ref at § 9.3 |
| Critical | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability: cap, mutuality, carve-outs | Deviation | § 21.1 (with §§ 21.2–21.4, 1.5) |
| Critical | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | Compliant | §§ 14.1–14.4, 15.1, 13.2 |
| High | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity binding Customer | Deviation | § 2.2 (conflicts with § 12.3) |
| High | MINCOMMIT — Minimum purchase commitments | Deviation | § 2.1 (conflicts with §§ 7.1, 9.4, 12.3) |
| High | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete binding Customer | Deviation | § 12.4 (conflicts with § 12.3) |
| High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | Deviation | § 13.1 (contradicts §§ 13.2–13.3) |
| High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | Compliant | §§ 24.1–24.4, 13.3 |
| High | LD — Liquidated damages / penalties on Customer | Compliant | §§ 9.4, 27.3, 7.3, 24.4 |
| High | T4C — Termination for convenience | Compliant | § 9.4 |
| Medium | TRANSITION — Transition assistance and data return | Deviation | § 11.1 (contradicts §§ 11.2–11.3) |
| Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | Deviation | § 19.2 (with §§ 19.1, 19.4, 6.1) |
| Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | Compliant | §§ 22.1–22.3 |
| Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | Compliant | §§ 28.1–28.3 |
| Medium | MFN — Most-favoured-nation obligations | Compliant | §§ 12.3, 7.1, 8.3 |
| Medium | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation binding Customer | Needs review (verification fail) | § 12.3 (and § 12.4) |
| Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and non-renewal notice | Compliant | §§ 8.2–8.3 |
| Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | Compliant | §§ 18.1–18.2 |

---

## Walk-away items

The following findings sit in walk-away territory under the playbook and must be resolved before signature:

1. **No Vendor indemnity; one-way Customer indemnity (§ 20.1).** No Vendor IP indemnity at all, plus a Customer indemnity for "every claim relating in any way to Customer's use of the Services." *Proposal:* insert the preferred Vendor indemnity (IP infringement, breach of law, Vendor-caused data breach, gross negligence/wilful misconduct) with notice/control/cooperation procedure, standard exclusions and procure/modify/replace/refund remedies — which also repairs the § 9.3 cross-reference — and narrow Customer's indemnity to Customer-provided content and Customer's breach of Applicable Law.
2. **One-month liability cap applied "without exception" (§ 21.1).** Below even the six-month walk-away threshold, on a Fee base that excludes the implementation charge (§ 1.5), and it caps the § 21.3 Excluded Claims (including indemnities) with no super-cap. *Proposal:* mutual greater-of 12 months' Fees / USD 1,000,000 cap, with Excluded Claims uncapped; §§ 21.2–21.4 stand.
3. **Full-term sole-source obligation (§ 2.2).** No category limit, no 12-month cap, no performance-based exit. *Proposal:* delete and confirm our freedom to source from third parties, aligning with § 12.3. *Fallback if pressed:* a single defined product category, 12 months, terminating automatically on any SLA or delivery failure.
4. **Three-year USD 2,000,000/year take-or-pay "without reduction or termination rights" (§ 2.1).** *Proposal:* delete; Fees payable only for Services ordered or used. *Fallback:* a single 12-month commitment, reducible on 30 days' notice, with a true-up rather than a penalty.
5. **24-month worldwide post-term non-compete (§ 12.4).** Undefined competitive scope, no carve-out for internal development or acquisitions. *Proposal:* delete, leaving § 12.3 to govern.
6. **Services licence revocable at Vendor's discretion and excluding Affiliates and contractors (§ 13.1).** *Proposal:* conform § 13.1 to the language already agreed in §§ 13.2–13.3 — extend to Affiliates and contractors acting on our behalf, delete discretionary revocation, and cross-reference the § 13.3 transfer and revocation limits.
7. **Immediate cessation of assistance and permanent deletion of Customer Data (§ 11.1).** *Proposal:* replace with up to six months of transition assistance at then-current rates plus export/migration support, with deletion governed by §§ 11.2–11.3.

---

## Next steps

1. **Issue the redline** on the eight deviations, leading with the two critical items (§§ 20 and 21.1) and the four Customer-side restrictions (§§ 2.1, 2.2, 12.4, 13.1).
2. **Frame the restriction edits as conformity fixes.** Sections 2.1, 2.2, 12.4 and 13.1 each contradict language Vendor has already accepted (§ 12.3, §§ 13.2–13.3), as do §§ 11.1 and 19.2 (§§ 11.2–11.3, §§ 19.1/19.4). There is no order-of-precedence clause to resolve these conflicts, so they should be corrected on the face of the document.
3. **Extend the Deliverable warranty (§ 19.2)** from fifteen to ninety days and confirm it does not limit §§ 19.1 or 19.4; note that the current fifteen-day window expires with the fifteen-business-day acceptance period in § 6.1, leaving no post-acceptance warranty.
4. **Resolve the NOSOLICIT verification failure internally.** The absence of a non-solicit is the preferred outcome and § 12.3 affirmatively preserves our hiring freedom; the two automated checks fail as phrasing artefacts. We propose no redline, since satisfying the checks would require inserting a restriction on our own client. Recommend clearing the flag as a false positive.
5. **Defend the favourable clauses.** Hold § 12.3, §§ 13.2–13.3, § 9.4, §§ 11.2–11.3, §§ 21.2–21.4, § 24 and §§ 8.2–8.3 without change if Vendor seeks reciprocal trims.
6. **Confirm the negotiation posture.** Flag to the business that items 1–7 above are walk-away positions, and confirm which fallbacks (exclusivity and minimum commitment) they are prepared to authorise.
"}
